newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 21.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 21.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - The German advertising industry's growth is being stifled by increasingly fierce competition in the world market, the president of the German Association of Advertising Agencies (GWA) Lothar Leonhard says. Leonhard says although the German industry saw moderate growth last year, it paled in comparison to the worldwide boom, which was twice as strong. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Despite mounting competition between online services in Germany, the industry spends relatively meagre amounts on advertising, says media marketing company MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM). Online services only spent 7.6 million marks ($4.5 million) on advertising last year, MGM says basing its findings on a study it conducted. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Europe-wide television channel NBC Europe plans to offer German advertisers two broadcast minutes per hour, giving them access to about 16 million households in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, says MGM. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The Frankfurt Marketing Services fair, which will run from April 23-26, expects 900 exhibitors and between 18,000 and 20,000 visitors, says Michael Peters, managing director of the Messe Frankfurt GmbH convention centre. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - A German banking consortium led by Commerzbank AG is ready to lend 1.5 billion marks to Bavarian media group Kirch Gruppe, newsmagazine Der Spiegel reports. A Commerzbank spokesman said he could not comment on the report. (Reuter)

BERLIN - The son of media mogul Leo Kirch plans to take over local Berlin broadcaster FAB, newsmagazine Focus and newspaper Tagesspiegel report. Thomas Kirch intends to invest a total of 80 million marks in Berlin and has also expressed interest in obtaining a majority holding in Berlin television channel Puls TV, the publications report. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Germany ranks as Europe's largest online service market, MGM says in its study, with 1.1 million households connected to an online service and four million users across the country. (Reuter)
BONN - The state of Bavaria plans to stop contributing funds to struggling public broadcaster ARD in 2001, says premiere Edmund Stoiber in the newspaper Welt am Sonntag. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - As music video channel Viva wins far more viewers in Germany than its chief competitor, MTV, Viva general manager Dieter Gorny anticipates MTV owner Viacom to pump funds into the German market to take over the top spot. (Handelsblatt)
MUNICH - A unit of the Kirch-Gruppe, BetaFilma, has won the German broadcasting rights for Michael Jackson's current tour. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN/WASHINGTON - A spokeswoman for the U.S. Commerce Department, Charlene Barshefsky, says the U.S. is concerned about whether the privatisation of the German telecommunications market complies with World Trade Organsation agreements. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Telephone company Otelo plans to turn to the federal post ministry to resolve its dispute with telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom over network access, newspaper Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Adalbert Lechner, 36, has taken over as managing director of confectionary company Aachener Schokoladen-Anbieters. Lechner was previously with Lindt chocolate maker in Austria. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Kurt Filip, 48, has replaced Dominico Madile as managing director of media agency Equmedia. (Reuter)
